Triggers.value: Undergoing a medical examination or procedure

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I think about how life would have been different if the event had not occurred
go along with whatever others want to feel safe
Being reminded of the event by others

Threat.value: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard

Memory.value: When I try to deliberately remember what happened I find it difficult to access the memory
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

Negative Appraisals.value: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it
I feel like an object, not like a person

vignette: As a child, Leila had grown accustomed to the sound of her mother's footsteps outside her bedroom door, signaling the start of another painful and humiliating encounter. The physical abuse she endured at the hands of her caregiver left an indelible mark on her psyche, shaping her perception of safety, trust, and self-worth. Years later, as a 24-year-old urban planner, Leila found herself navigating a world where medical procedures and somatic sensations like nausea could transport her back to those terrifying moments. The mere thought of undergoing a medical examination or procedure made her feel like she was reliving the trauma all over again. When she felt nauseous, it was as if her body was reminding her of the helplessness she had experienced as a child. Leila's mind would often wander to counterfactual thoughts - "What if my mother had been different? What if I had grown up in a loving home?" - as a way to cope with the overwhelming emotions that came flooding back. She also found herself people-pleasing, going along with whatever others wanted, just to feel safe and avoid conflict. When reminded of the event by others, she would become withdrawn and evasive, desperate to avoid any conversation that might bring up painful memories. Leila struggled to recall the details of her childhood trauma deliberately, as if her mind was actively working to suppress those memories. However, when fragments did surface, they were often accompanied by intense rage - a feeling she couldn't quite understand or articulate. Sometimes, she would experience the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory, leaving her feeling disoriented and lost. The injustice of what had happened to her weighed heavily on Leila's mind, fueling a deep-seated sense of dehumanization - as if she was nothing more than an object, not a person worthy of love or respect. She believed herself to be weak, unable to stand up for herself or assert her needs. When faced with triggers like medical procedures or somatic sensations, Leila's mind would immediately turn to those maladaptive strategies - people-pleasing, counterfactual thinking, and avoidance. These coping mechanisms provided temporary relief but ultimately reinforced the very negative appraisals that had taken hold of her life. Her perception of injustice and dehumanization would intensify, leading her to feel like she was walking on eggshells, constantly anticipating the next threat. As Leila navigated her daily environment - designing urban spaces meant to promote safety and community - she found herself becoming increasingly vigilant, hyper-aware of potential dangers lurking around every corner. Sudden movements by others put her immediately on guard, making it difficult for her to concentrate or feel at ease in public spaces. Her "safe zone" had shrunk to the point where she only felt secure in a handful of places - her apartment, her car, and certain secluded areas in nature. Leila's memories, though fragmented, continued to exert a profound impact on her life. When they surfaced, they brought with them a tidal wave of emotions - rage, shame, and fear - that left her reeling. Her maladaptive strategies would kick into high gear, reinforcing the negative appraisals that had become entrenched in her psyche. As Leila struggled to break free from this cycle, she found herself wondering if she would ever be able to shake off the weight of her childhood trauma. Would she ever feel like a whole person again - capable of trust, intimacy, and joy? For now, those questions hung in the balance, as she tentatively began to seek help and confront the demons that had haunted her for so long.
